refnamediv.refpurpose: An API for acquiring a pseudo-terminal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: io.systemd.PTYBroker is a Varlink interface implemented by systemd1-related components. It can be introspected and called with varlinkctl1.

The broker hands out pseudo-terminal (PTY) pairs and tracks them across processes. AcquirePty() allocates a new PTY pair, optionally backed by a command line or an interactive shell (viaShell), and returns file descriptors for the frontend (the caller's side) and the backend, plus the unit that runs the backend. EnrollPty() adopts an already existing PTY pair. ListPty(), ConfigurePty(), MonitorPty() and HangUpPty() inspect, reconfigure, monitor and terminate tracked PTYs. TerminalSettings carries the window size, the terminal type and similar per-PTY state.

FrontendType selects what happens with the frontend (master) side: hand the file descriptor to the caller (take), read from it and forward the output to monitors and discard it (null), or additionally log it (log). BackendType selects whether the backend (slave) side is handed to the caller as well (take) or whether the broker invokes a shell on it (shell). WorkingDirectory names the initial directory for such a shell, either as an absolute path or as the home directory of the user, and ProcessId refers to a process by PID, together with the pidfdId/bootId pair that disambiguates it across PID reuse.

Names are unique: PtyExists is returned if a name is taken, NoSuchPty if the named PTY is unknown, TooManyPtys and TooManyMonitors when local limits are reached, and TrackingNotEnabled if the broker was started without PTY tracking. This is the mechanism systemd-run1 and PID 1 use to attach a PTY to a service.

refsect1.title: Security
refsect1.para: The interface is served by systemd-ptybrokerd.service8 on the /run/systemd/io.systemd.PTYBroker socket, which is world-connectable (SocketMode=0666); a per-user instance is available as %t/systemd/io.systemd.PTYBroker. Acquiring a PTY authenticates through the polkit action io.systemd.PTYBroker.acquire-pty, or io.systemd.PTYBroker.acquire-pty-with-shell when a shell backend is requested, and interactive authentication is requested when the caller sets allowInteractiveAuthentication. The matching polkit policy is installed with the service.

refsect1.title: Interface Definition
refsect1.para: The following interface definition is exposed:
refsect1.programlisting:
# An API for acquiring a pseudo-terminal # [Experimental] interface io.systemd.PTYBroker
# What to do with the PTY frontend. type FrontendType( # Return the file descriptor of the frontend side of the pty to the caller, do not keep a duplicate. take, # Read any data received from the backend and send it to monitors, afterwards discard it null, # Read any data received from the backend and write it to monitors and the logs log )
# What to do with the PTY backend. type BackendType( # Return the file descriptor of the backend side of the pty to the caller, do not keep a duplicate. take, # Invoke a shell on the backend side. shell )
# Details about terminal settings. type TerminalSettings( # Terminal type ($TERM) envTERM: ?string, # Terminal type ($COLORTERM) envCOLORTERM: ?string, # Whether $NO_COLOR is set to a non-empty value, i.e. color output shall be suppressed (see no-color.org) envNO_COLOR: ?bool, # Width (in character cell columns) for the pty columns: ?int, # Height (in character cell lines) for the pty lines: ?int )
# The working directory of the shell. type WorkingDirectory( # The path to the working directory. Mutually exclusive with 'home' path: ?string, # If true, use the configured user's home directory as the working directory. Mutually exclusive with 'path' home: ?bool, # Whether the path to the working directory is allowed to not exist missingOK: ?bool )
# An object for referencing UNIX processes type ProcessId( # Numeric UNIX PID value pid: int, # 64bit inode number of pidfd if known pidfdId: ?int, # Boot ID of the system the inode number belongs to bootId: ?string )
# Allocates a PTY pair, and configures what to do with each side. # [Supports 'upgrade' flag] method AcquirePty( # What to do with the 'frontend' of the pty, also known as the pty 'master' frontendType: FrontendType, # What to do with the 'backend' of the pty, also known the pty 'slave' backendType: BackendType, # A unique name to identify the pty allocation with name: ?string, # A descriptive string to identify the pty allocation with (doesn't have to be unique) description: ?string, # The syslog 'tag' to use for this pseudo TTY output when connected to logging tag: ?string, # For shell backend: user to run the shell as user: ?string, # For shell backend: group to run the shell as group: ?string, # For shell backend: initial directory for the shell, either an absolute path or the home directory of the user workingDirectory: ?WorkingDirectory, # For shell backend: environment variables for the shell, as a list of assignments in the usual VAR=VALUE syntax environment: ?[]string, # For shell backend: whether to allocate a 'lightweight' session lightweight: ?bool, # For shell backend: command line to invoke as main service process. If unset an interactive login shell is invoked. commandLine: ?[]string, # For shell backend: whether to invoke the command line via the target user's native shell. Defaults to true. If false a command line must be specified, and is invoked directly. viaShell: ?bool, # For shell backend: absolute path of the binary to execute. Only valid if viaShell is false. If unset the first element of the command line is used, otherwise the first element of the command line is only passed as argv[0] (e.g. to request login shell semantics by prefixing it with a dash). executable: ?string, # Convert the connection into a monitor connection once done monitor: ?bool, # If true, hang up the pty once this monitor connection is disconnected. If null defaults to false. hangUpOnDisconnect: ?bool, # If true, a hangup of the backend side of the pty (e.g. because the last process having it open closed it, or called vhangup() on it) does not release the pty, since the backend might be reopened later. Only valid in combination with the monitor and hangUpOnDisconnect flags, as the monitor connection going away then defines the lifetime of the pty. If null defaults to false. ignoreHangup: ?bool, # If true, track the dimensions of the monitor's terminal via OSC 2811 sequences on the monitor stream, and propagate the minimum dimensions of all monitors to the pty. Only valid in combination with the monitor flag. If null defaults to false. osc2811: ?bool, # Initial settings for the terminal terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # Selected name for the pty allocation name: string, # A descriptive string to identify the pty allocation with (doesn't have to be unique) description: ?string, # The frontend type for this PTY frontendType: FrontendType, # The backend type for this PTY backendType: BackendType, # The syslog 'tag' to use for this pseudo TTY output when connected to logging tag: ?string, # The index of the PTY frontend (i.e. 'master') frontendFileDescriptor: ?int, # The index of the PTY backend (i.e. 'slave') backendFileDescriptor: ?int, # The TTY path name of the allocate pseudo TTY backendPath: string, # The name of the transient service unit that runs the shell or login on the PTY backend side. unit: ?string, # Settled settings for the terminal terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings )
# Enrolls a pre-allocated PTY frontend (i.e. the master). # [Supports 'upgrade' flag] method EnrollPty( # The index of the PTY frontend (i.e. 'master') frontendFileDescriptor: int, # What to do with the 'frontend' of the pty, also known as the pty 'master' frontendType: FrontendType, # The TTY path name of the pre-allocated pseudo TTY, if known and meaningful to the broker. Leave unset if the path only makes sense within the caller's namespace. backendPath: ?string, # A unique name to identify the pty allocation with name: ?string, # A descriptive string to identify the pty allocation with (doesn't have to be unique) description: ?string, # The syslog 'tag' to use for this pseudo TTY output when connected to logging tag: ?string, # Convert the connection into a monitor connection once done monitor: ?bool, # If true, hang up the pty once this monitor connection is disconnected. If null defaults to false. hangUpOnDisconnect: ?bool, # If true, a hangup of the backend side of the pty (e.g. because the last process having it open closed it, or called vhangup() on it) does not release the pty, since the backend might be reopened later. Only valid in combination with the monitor and hangUpOnDisconnect flags, as the monitor connection going away then defines the lifetime of the pty. If null defaults to false. ignoreHangup: ?bool, # If true, track the dimensions of the monitor's terminal via OSC 2811 sequences on the monitor stream, and propagate the minimum dimensions of all monitors to the pty. Only valid in combination with the monitor flag. If null defaults to false. osc2811: ?bool, # Initial settings for the terminal terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # Selected name for the pty allocation name: string, # A descriptive string to identify the pty allocation with (doesn't have to be unique) description: ?string, # The frontend type for this PTY frontendType: FrontendType, # The backend type for this PTY backendType: BackendType, # The syslog 'tag' to use for this pseudo TTY output when connected to logging tag: ?string, # Settled settings for the terminal terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings )
# Monitor frontend side of the pty. # [Requires 'upgrade' flag] method MonitorPty( # The name of the PTY allocation to connect to. name: string, # How many lines of track buffer to return. If null defaults to 0. trackBufferLines: ?int, # If true, hang up the pty once this monitor connection is disconnected. If null defaults to false. hangUpOnDisconnect: ?bool, # If true, track the dimensions of the monitor's terminal via OSC 2811 sequences on the monitor stream, and propagate the minimum dimensions of all monitors to the pty. If null defaults to false. osc2811: ?bool, # New settings for the terminal (not that the environment based settings will not be propagated to the backend processes) terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # Name of the allocated PTY name: string, # A descriptive string to identify the pty allocation with (doesn't have to be unique) description: ?string, # The frontend type for this PTY frontendType: FrontendType, # The backend type for this PTY backendType: BackendType, # The syslog 'tag' to use for this pseudo TTY output when connected to logging tag: ?string, # The TTY path name of the allocate pseudo TTY backendPath: ?string, # The unit backing the PTY if known unit: ?string, # Current contents of the track buffer, line by line. trackBuffer: ?[]string, # Settings for the terminal terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings )
# Reconfigure pseudo terminal method ConfigurePty( # The name of the PTY allocation to reconfigure to. name: string, # New settings for the terminal (not that the environment based settings will not be propagated to the backend processes) terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # Complete configured settings terminalSettings: ?TerminalSettings )
# List allocated pseudo-terminals # [Supports 'more' flag] method ListPty( # The name of the PTY allocation to list. name: ?string, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # Name of the allocated PTY name: string, # A descriptive string to identify the pty allocation with (doesn't have to be unique) description: ?string, # The frontend type for this PTY frontendType: FrontendType, # The backend type for this PTY backendType: BackendType, # The syslog 'tag' to use for this pseudo TTY output when connected to logging tag: ?string, # The backend path for this PTY backendPath: ?string, # The unit backing the PTY if known unit: ?string, # The process of the client that allocated this PTY owner: ?ProcessId, # The UID of the client that allocated this PTY ownerUID: ?int, # The GID of the client that allocated this PTY ownerGID: ?int )
# Hang up pseudo terminal method HangUpPty( # Name of the allocated PTY to hang up name: string, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ()
# No PTY by the given name known error NoSuchPty()
# A PTY by the given name already exists. error PtyExists()
# Limit on number of PTYs reached. error TooManyPtys()
# Limit on number of monitors of a PTY reached. error TooManyMonitors()
# Tracking of PTY state not enabled for specified PTY. error TrackingNotEnabled()

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.para: varlinkctl introspect SERVICE io.systemd.PTYBroker shows the interface definition as served by SERVICE, and varlinkctl call SERVICE io.systemd.PTYBroker.AcquirePty \ '{"frontendType": "take", "backendType": "take"}' invokes its AcquirePty() method.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: The io.systemd.PTYBroker interface was added in version 263.

AcquirePty(), BackendType, ConfigurePty(), EnrollPty(), FrontendType, HangUpPty(), ListPty(), MonitorPty(), NoSuchPty, ProcessId, PtyExists, TerminalSettings, TooManyMonitors, TooManyPtys, TrackingNotEnabled, and WorkingDirectory were added in version 263.
